<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="BRPXQZME" />{{running header|{{smaller|{{asc|ODE 7.}}}}|{{asc|THE MAJOR ODES OF THE KINGDOM.}}|391}}{{rule}}</noinclude><ref follow="p390_3">to the [[Portal:Shang dynasty|dynasty of Shang]], and his making all the states under his presidency loyal also.</ref>virtue left nothing to be dissatisfied with,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He received the blessing of God,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And it was extended to his descendants.

God said to king Wăn<ref>The statement that 'God spake to [[w:King Wen of Zhou|king Wăn]],' repeated in stanza 7, vexes the Chinese critics, and they find in it simply an intimation that Wăn's conduct was 'in accordance with the will of Heaven.' I am not prepared to object to that view of the meaning; but it is plain that the writer, in giving such a form to his meaning, must have conceived of God as a personal Being, knowing men's hearts, and able to influence them.</ref>,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
'Be not like those who reject this and cling to that;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Be not like those who are ruled by their likings and desires;'{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
So he grandly ascended before others to the height (of virtue).{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The people of {{tooltip|Mî|Mì}}<ref>[[w:zh:密須|Mî]] or [[w:Lingtai County|Mî-hsü]] was a state in the present [[w:Jingning County, Gansu|''K''ing-ning ''K''âu]], of [[w:Pingliang|Phing-liang]] department, [[w:Gansu|Kan-sû]].</ref> were disobedient,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Daring to oppose our great country,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And invaded {{tooltip|Yüan|Ruǎn}}, marching to {{tooltip|Kung|Gōng}}<ref>[[wikt:阮|Yüan]] was a state adjacent to [[w:zh:密須|Mî]],—the present [[w:Jingchuan County|''K''ing ''K''âu]], and [[wikt:共|Kung]] must have been a place or district in it.</ref>.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The king rose, majestic in his wrath;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He marshalled his troops,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
To stop the invading foes;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
To consolidate the prosperity of {{tooltip|''K''âu}};{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
To meet the expectations of all under heaven.

He remained quietly in the capital,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
But (his troops) went on from the borders of Yüan.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
They ascended our lofty ridges,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And (the enemy) arrayed no forces on our hills,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
On our hills, small or large,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Nor drank at our springs,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Our springs or our pools.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He then determined the finest of the plains,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And settled on the south of {{tooltip|''Kh''î|Qí}}<ref>[[w:King Wen of Zhou|Wăn]], it appears, made now a small change in the site of his capital, but did not move to [[w:Fengjing (Zhou)|Făng]], where he finally settled.</ref>,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
On the banks of<noinclude><!--¶-->
